claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me begin with a few key questions.

**First, could you tell me the names and dates of birth of the children you're enquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He was born in March 2009, so he's 16 now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're enquiring about Child Benefit for your son Alex, who was born in March 2009 and is currently 16 years old.

Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about Alex's current circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Thank you for confirming that Alex is in full-time education.

Now I need to gather some information about your own circumstances to complete the eligibility assessment.

**What is your residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status or another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, yes. I live here in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that information.

I have one more important question to help me assess your eligibility:

**Are you currently receiving any of the following benefits: Jobseeker's Allowance, Employment and Support Allowance, Incapacity Benefit, Severe Disablement Allowance, or Pension Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key details:
- **Child:** Alex, born March 2009 (currently 16 years old)
- **Your status:** British citizen, resident in England
- **Alex's status:** In full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- **Your benefit status:** Not receiving the listed out-of-work benefits

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I can now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Excellent news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:
- Alex is under 19 years old and in full-time education, which means he qualifies for Child Benefit
- You have the appropriate residency status as a British citizen living in England
- You're not receiving any of the benefits that would cause issues with your eligibility

You should be able to proceed with your Child Benefit claim. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, please let me know!
